summary: Shasta County steel tower the register dates to 1982, designed by CDF engineer Mike Plesha; the sources disagree on whether a lookout still stands, and the site is now a radio and repeater site.

facts.design: CDF Plan No. 1559-2A steel tower with a 732-6A Plesha-design cab; hollow steel legs originally intended for atomic test towers
facts.status_note: The register says only the tower remains; a 2012 FFLA report says the lookout no longer exists and the site is a repeater site. The FFLA California list marks it Standing*, which its key defines as a tower with the cab no longer in place.
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Shasta-Trinity Unit (Cal Fire)

access.note: Register (1991 access note) says the site is accessible to the public, 6.7 miles from paved road. Radio site with very high electromagnetic radiation near the catwalk; do not climb.

notes_for_editor: Status is disputed and not resolved. The register says the tower remains, the FFLA California list marks it Standing*, which its key defines as a tower with the cab no longer in place, and the FFLA 2012 chapter report says the site no longer exists and is a repeater site. The register's text is internally inconsistent about the cab: a 732-6A cab tops the tower with a repeater antenna attached, yet the cabin and storage structure are said to be removed. The FFLA key therefore adds a cab-gone reading that conflicts with the register's 732-6A entry; the sources do not settle it. The 1977 newspaper item predates the 1982 build date, so an earlier lookout may have stood here; the sources do not say. The access note is from 1991. The site carries high RF exposure; the story advises against climbing. One web search added only CEQA notices and a repeater reference.
